questions.stem: A 12 year old girl attends her school vaccination session with her mother. She is well and has no medical problems. She receives the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine. Her mother asks how this fits into her daughter's long-term health care.
questions.q: Which level of prevention does this intervention represent?
questions.e: Vaccination prevents HPV infection, and so cervical cancer, before disease occurs: primary prevention.

steps.x: The question asks: Which level of prevention does this intervention represent?
A healthy child receiving a vaccine before any disease exists.

elim: Primordial prevention targets the social conditions that create risk factors in whole populations.
Quaternary prevention protects patients from over-medicalisation and unnecessary intervention.
Secondary prevention detects existing disease early, for example screening.
Tertiary prevention reduces complications of established disease.

steps.x: Primary = prevent disease occurring (vaccines, smoking cessation).

questions.stem: A 65 year old man is invited by letter for a one-off abdominal ultrasound. He has no symptoms and his abdomen is soft and non-tender. The scan shows an infrarenal aortic diameter of 3.6 cm and he is entered into surveillance.
questions.q: Which level of prevention does this programme represent?
questions.e: Screening finds existing but asymptomatic disease early so it can be managed before rupture: secondary prevention.

steps.x: The question asks: Which level of prevention does this programme represent?
Detecting an asymptomatic aneurysm that is already there.

elim: Primary prevention stops disease before it occurs, for example vaccination or smoking cessation.
Primordial prevention targets the social conditions that create risk factors in whole populations.
Quaternary prevention protects patients from over-medicalisation and unnecessary intervention.
Tertiary prevention reduces complications of established disease.

steps.x: Secondary = early detection of existing disease (screening).

questions.stem: A 59 year old woman has had type 2 diabetes for 8 years and had a stroke last year. She attends a community stroke rehabilitation programme with physiotherapy and speech therapy, and her GP reviews her HbA1c and blood pressure every 3 months to prevent further complications.
questions.q: Which level of prevention do these interventions represent?
questions.e: Rehabilitation and chronic disease control in established disease reduce complications and disability: tertiary prevention.

steps.x: The question asks: Which level of prevention do these interventions represent?
Disease is already established; the aim is to limit its consequences.

elim: Primary prevention stops disease before it occurs, for example vaccination or smoking cessation.
Primordial prevention targets the social conditions that create risk factors in whole populations.
Quaternary prevention protects patients from over-medicalisation and unnecessary intervention.
Secondary prevention detects existing disease early, for example screening.

steps.x: Tertiary = reduce complications of established disease (rehab, chronic disease control).

questions.stem: A 29 year old woman attends for her first cervical screening. She has no symptoms. The laboratory reports that her sample is inadequate and cannot be tested. This is the first inadequate result she has had. Her cervix looked normal at the time of sampling.
